text:
anna: quick sync — I sketched a proposal for a dynamic sampling controller in the OTLP pipeline to handle head/tail sampling by route and customer tier. posting so we can iterate.
kevin: nice, can you summarize the goals? short bullets pls.
sophie: main ask from product was: keep error-debug traces for high-value customers, throttle noisy low-tier routes, and avoid losing tail errors for things we don't yet know are important.
anna: exactly. goals: 1) keep representative tail traces for global visibility, 2) deterministic head sampling for low-cost metrics, 3) per-tenant overrides for high-tier customers, 4) ability to change sampling rates realtime via console/UI without redeploys.
mike: operational constraints? where does the sampling decision live — collector, agent, or ingest service?
anna: tradeoffs: collector-side (otel-collector) is easiest to roll out across private/dedicated/hosted, but per-tenant decisions need tenant metadata attached to spans. ingest-side gives more context (route, customer signals) but increases egress cost.
kevin: my concern with collector-side is lack of full business context for tail sampling (we might only know a span is slow after correlating many spans). tail sampling ideally needs a short window store.
sophie: agreed — we should do hybrid: cheap deterministic head sampling at edge/agent (by route hash + tier), and a tail-sample candidate stream forwarded with minimal index info to a small windowing service that makes finalize/keep decisions.
anna: prototype topology I put in the doc:

```
[edge agent] -> head sampler (per-route deterministic) -> ingest (metrics + low-res traces)
                         
                          -> tail-candidate stream -> tail controller (5s window) -> keep/drop decision -> long-term trace store/exporters

controller exposes API for dynamic rules: {route, customer_tier, min_error_rate, min_latency_ms, keep_rate}
```

mike: windowing service + controller seems fine. what's our retention/cost target for kept traces? We need rough numbers to show finance.
anna: proposal: baseline keep_rate 0.5% cross-tenant for tails, 100% for p1 customers, and route-specific overrides. retention for kept full traces = 30 days by default. metrics and low-res sampled traces -> 90 days.
kevin: 0.5% global might still be heavy for noisy routes. we should add per-route cap and adaptive downsampling: if a route generates >X tps, apply extra throttling.
sophie: yep also add a simple backpressure signal to the controller from exporters (if write queue > 80%) to reduce tail candidate retention 
anna: good call. also need to ensure deterministic sampling uses a stable hash so replayed requests sample consistently across retries. use trace_id or request_id fallback.
kevin: how do we surface this in console? product wants a rollout UX where ops can set rules and preview estimated cost impact before applying.
mike: show estimated token/spans/GB impact, and an expected saved latency percent for traces. a preview simulation over a recent 1h sample would be perfect.
anna: plan for console: rules DSL, preview panel with estimated kept trace count and expected monthly storage, and a quick rollback toggle. ops can scope rules to route patterns, org IDs, or tags.
kevin: metrics to drive alerts: keep_rate per-route, tail-controller backlog, dropped-kept-ratio, exporter write latency.
sophie: we also need to ensure correlation ids (request.route, customer.tier) are propagated through SDKs. add to docs and default SDK tags.
anna: open question: exporters. we should keep a small "full-trace" queue to the long-term store (e.g., honeycomb/tempo) and an aggregated stream to metrics backend. do we want per-tenant splitter in collector or centralized?
mike: split at collector so we can apply quick denies for compliance-sensitive tenants (private deploys). centralized split is simpler for hosted but harder for private.
kevin: sounds like we need the same abstraction in all deployments: collector plugin that enforces the rules but controller can be hosted or local depending on deployment mode.
sophie: security note: any dynamic rules API must be authenticated and auditable. store rule diffs in audit log and show in console.
anna: implementation milestones I proposed: 1) add deterministic head sampler to agents (2 weeks), 2) tail-candidate stream + small controller prototype (3 weeks), 3) integration with console preview + rules UI (2 sprints), 4) rollout to staging + A/B test on a few routes (1 sprint).
kevin: timeline reasonable. can we ship a simple opt-in flag on staging first to collect telemetry for the preview?
anna: yes — collectors will emit a "candidate_count" and sample-simulation feed to a preview indexer. that lets console run cost estimates.
mike: one more: retention + compliance. for private deployments, need an opt-out that never sends tails off-host. make that a per-tenant policy.
sophie: logging side: ensure we link retained traces to logs by request_id. also add a small index artifact to speed UI preview queries (store metadata separate).
anna: last: ops fallback behavior: if controller is unreachable, fall back to static conservative sampling (e.g., 0.1% tails for non-P1). infra-bot, can we add that as a deploy checklist?
infra-bot: noted. added task #4672 to rollout checklist: "ensure controller fallback policy configured" :white_check_mark:
kevin: thanks everyone — can we take disagreements to the doc? I'll add comments inline on head vs collector split.
sophie: I'll update SDK tagging tasks.
mike: I'll draft the cost model numbers and share tomorrow.
anna: thanks — i'll post the design doc link in #eng-architecture after I update with today's notes. :rocket: otel-bot: OTEL-TRACE: candidate_stream_created route=/api/generate tenant=acme count=462
anna: (end)
